chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who deliberately broke his fast for one day in the month of Ramadan without an excuse. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should emancipate a slave, or fast two consecutive months, or feed sixty poor people. If he is not able, he should give in charity with whatever he can afford.'
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for deliberately breaking a fast in Ramadan without an excuse?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the hierarchical expiation (kaffarah) for deliberately breaking the Ramadan fast, prioritizing freeing a slave, then fasting two consecutive months, and finally feeding sixty poor people if unable to fast. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes a structured progression of financial and physical sacrifice, reflecting the severity of the breach. The requirement for 'consecutive' days in the fasting option underscores the continuity of devotion required to atone for the interruption of the holy month.
